A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M3DLayout dataset and generation benchmarks. Their complete main texts, supplementary material, tables, figures, and equations support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original dataset statistics, generation benchmarks, training-source ablations, efficiency measurements, and a 42-participant perceptual study.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and additionally reports dataset complexity/diversity measurements and human evaluation of 1,000 dataset scenes.

M1.justification: The dataset-construction pipeline, diffusion and autoregressive models, objectives, and retrieval procedure remain unchanged. Section 9.2 clarifies the existing omission of shape codes and specifies the existing IoU penalty; it does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain M3DLayout's 3D-FRONT, Matterport3D, and Inf3DLayout sources, room coverage, and text-conditioned layout-generation task. The added dataset audits analyze retained data rather than introduce another domain or generation test scenario.

E2.justification: DiffuScene and InstructScene remain the evaluated comparison methods. v3 Table 4 juxtaposes DiffuScene scores already in v2 Table 3 with the 3D-FRONT-trained diffusion model scores already in v2 Table 5; this redisplay does not establish an additional evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: v3 Section 10 introduces substantial dataset-validation protocols: additional complexity measures, diversity evaluation using 500 scenes, and a 1,000-scene human audit with approximately 200 evaluators, three five-point criteria, and two independent ratings per scene. Existing generation splits, training budgets, 1,500 test prompts, and the original perceptual-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 10 directly examines dataset complexity, category/geometric/semantic diversity, layout rationality, and description accuracy. These analyses substantially expand validation beyond v2's descriptive statistics and generated-layout user study. The existing training-source ablations and density-control examples are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 6 retains its existing error bars, and neither version supplies training-seed or repeated-run counts. The added audit reports means and threshold proportions without confidence intervals, significance tests, or quantified inter-rater uncertainty. Its double-rating consistency procedure adds study-design information rather than a specified uncertainty estimator.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial dataset-validation results. Table 6 reports, for example, category entropy of 0.635 versus 0.720 and CLIP distance of 0.133 versus 0.203 for 3D-FRONT versus M3DLayout. Section 10.2 reports mean human ratings of 4.423, 4.462, and 4.436, with corresponding scores-at-least-four rates of 94.05%, 94.08%, and 93.84%. Existing generation, efficiency, and ablation scores are unchanged; Table 4 reuses earlier results.

T1.justification: Section 10.1 introduces a mathematical definition of the new dataset-level semantic-diversity statistic, D_text, as mean pairwise cosine distance between normalized text embeddings. The core generative equations remain unchanged, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the 21,367-layout multi-source dataset, the detailed Inf3DLayout subset, and diffusion/autoregressive benchmarks demonstrating richer, text-controllable layouts. Additional validation supports these retained claims without redefining their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the added audits as supporting dataset quality and explains that shape codes are omitted because Matterport scans lack complete object shapes. It also removes v2's conclusion warning that language-model-generated descriptions may contain noise. Existing explanations of generation performance and generalization remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the axis-aligned IoU calculation and explicitly documents training without shape-code embeddings. Its abstract replaces the future data/code-release promise with a statement of release and a repository link. Existing architecture, optimizer, learning-rate, and split details are retained; the original study's explicit lack-of-compensation disclosure is removed.

R1.justification: The same 41 cited works are retained. Section 9.2 adds a more explicit relationship to DiffuScene, identifying shape-code use as the key distinction and describing similar performance under 3D-FRONT training. Broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and narrative organization are retained. Local edits rename Section 2.2, remove a repetitive related-work paragraph, streamline the user-study and conclusion text, add acknowledgements and a dataset-analysis section, and update the supplementary overview. The fidelity/controllability wording is corrected to match the already-existing appendix definitions.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 4 to consolidate existing comparison scores and Table 6 for new dataset metrics. Existing tables are retained with renumbering; Figure 4 is reformatted and Figure 5 moves from PDF page 8 to page 7. The existing qualitative examples and all 13 figures remain.

improvement.justification: The added human audit provides direct quantitative support for dataset annotation and layout quality beyond v2's unspecified sampled manual review. Implementation clarifications and release information also help reproducibility. These gains are limited by an unexplained discrepancy: new Table 6 assigns M3DLayout 26.8 objects per scene, while retained Table 1 gives 20.3 overall and 26.8 for Inf3DLayout. Removing the annotation-noise warning also weakens qualification. The principal generation results remain unchanged.
